To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the best note-taking strategy for college students is to encode and review one’s own notes and the least effective strategy is to encode and mentally review one’s own or an externally provided notes.

(a) students who took notes and reviewed their own notes recalled the most information; (b) students who listened to the lecture and reviewed their own outlines recalled the least; (c) students who listened and reviewed their notes recalled more than those who listened and reviewed the professor’s outline; and (d) students who listened, took notes, and reviewed the professor's outline recalled more information than those who listened to the professor's outline and reviewed their notes.

students who encode and review either their own notes or an external outline produced by the professor perform best, whereas students who either encode or review either their own lecture notes or an external lecture outline produced by the professors perform worst.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of note-taking on the retention of lecture materials.
the effects of encoding and an external memory device (notes or outline) on note-taking and review.
how students can take the best notes and how they can best use them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most effective note-taking method for college students involves a combination of encoding the lecture and reviewing either one's own notes or a lecture outline.
students should personally encode the lecture and review their own notes.
the best method for note taking and reviewing would include both encoding and an external memory device, and that the best type of external memory device would be a personally prepared one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
students should not be allowed to take notes on the lecture.
the most effective method for taking notes is to encode the lecture and then use the notes or an outline to review the material.
the best way for students to take notes is to personally encode the lecture while taking notes and then to review those notes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
students should take notes in class and then review their notes.
note-taking is an effective study strategy, and it is best to use it in combination with other effective strategies, like summarizing and outlining.
students should take notes during lectures and review them afterwards.
